assertions.assertion: Explains that SLO uses front-channel logout via iframes (not redirect chains)
assertions.rationale: Lines 4-5 explicitly state 'Duende IdentityServer implements front-channel Single Logout via iframes, not redirect chains.' The flow description (lines 8-15) further details iframe usage.

assertions.assertion: Shows SingleLogoutServiceUrls configuration with SamlEndpointType and SamlBinding.HttpRedirect
assertions.rationale: Lines 58-65 show `SingleLogoutServiceUrls` configured with `new SamlEndpointType { Location = ..., Binding = SamlBinding.HttpRedirect }`.

assertions.assertion: Mentions that partial logout is normal/expected when some SPs don't respond
assertions.rationale: Lines 17-18 state 'Partial logout is normal and expected — some SPs may not respond to the iframe requests'. The pitfalls table at line 227 also notes 'This is expected. Front-channel SLO is best-effort.'
Lines 119-168 have a dedicated section 'Distributed Deployments: ISamlLogoutSessionStore' explaining its use for multi-node deployments and showing both EF Core and custom Redis implementations.
